_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: the 2026-08-14 onboarding of the upstream unifi print (printing-press 4.30.1, contributed by Ricardo Cabral / @phoenix-server) into msp-skills as unifi-network. Every entry corrects a claim or value that the generated tree got wrong; the adversarial review that caught the topology claim is the reason this ledger exists.

handfixes.summary: topology is described as the device-to-client tree it actually builds, not a gateway-to-switch-to-AP physical tree
handfixes.why: The generated description (in the Cobra Short, the root --help highlights, the `which` feature index, the MCP feature list, SKILL.md and guide.md) claimed topology shows 'the physical device tree (gateway to switches to APs)'. The command's own Long description contradicts that: 'The API's device-list response does not include device-to-device uplink chaining (that only appears on a per-device detail fetch), so a switch-behind-switch or AP-behind-switch relationship is not shown - every device is listed at the top level.' topology.go groups clients under their uplinkDeviceId, producing a two-level device-to-client tree. Shipping the original wording would have promised a network map the command cannot draw. If a reprint restores the phrase 'physical device tree', the claim is false again.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The novel-feature description in .printing-press.json was written from the feature's intent rather than its implemented behaviour, and the press propagated it to six surfaces. A reprint should regenerate these strings from the corrected .printing-press.json novel_features entry.

asserts.contains: Group every synced client under the device it is attached to
Group every synced client under the device it is attached to
which clients sit behind which device
Group every synced client under the device it is attached to

handfixes.summary: drift's one-line description says the baseline is the last drift run, not the last sync
handfixes.why: The generated Short said drift shows what changed 'since the last sync snapshot'. drift.go's own Long says the comparison is 'against a snapshot captured the last time drift itself ran for this site' - running sync does not set or move the baseline. An agent that believed the Short would run sync, then drift, and report the diff as covering the sync window.

asserts.contains: since the last drift run for this site
since the last drift run for this site

handfixes.summary: sites devices adopt's example passes a MAC address, not a street address
handfixes.why: The generated example was `--mac-address 123 Test St, Anytown, ST 12345` - a mock-value collision that put a postal address in a MAC field. Copy-pasteable examples are the first thing an agent tries.

handfixes.summary: user-facing strings say UniFi, not Unifi
handfixes.why: The generated root Short/Long, the auth command's Short, and the MCP server name used 'Unifi'. The vendor's brand is UniFi; the mis-cased form appeared in the first line of --help.

handfixes.summary: var version is 0.0.0-dev, not the upstream public-library release number
handfixes.why: The vendored tree carried `var version = "2026.8.1"`, the version this CLI was released under in mvanhorn/printing-press-library. In msp-skills the release workflow injects the tag version via ldflags (-X <module>/internal/cli.version=), and every other connector ships 0.0.0-dev as the source default. Leaving 2026.8.1 in makes an unreleased local build claim a version that does not correspond to any msp-skills tag.

handfixes.summary: the `api` command's hint text names unifi-network-cli, not the nonexistent unifi-cli
handfixes.why: api_discovery.go hardcoded the bare slug string "unifi" in three Fprintf/Errorf calls that build '%s-cli ...', so `api` printed copy-pasteable hints for a binary named `unifi-cli` - which does not exist; the binary is `unifi-network-cli`. It survived the -pp- strip because the literal is the bare original slug, not a -pp- suffixed name, so no rename rule matched it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The press should derive this hint from the CLI's own binary name (os.Args[0] or the generated cliName const) rather than baking the slug in as a literal.

handfixes.summary: the MCP tenant gate falls through to the tool handler when no platform source is registered, instead of default-denying every non-mirror tool
handfixes.why: cli.VerifyMCPInvocation returns (nil, nil) when registeredPlatformSource is nil, which means 'there is nothing to gate' - and no connector in this repo registers a platform source (registerPlatformSource has zero callers outside internal/cli/platform_client.go). The 4.30.1/4.30.2 gate read that nil session as a failure and answered 'MCP tenant gate is not configured' for every tool that is not a Cobra mirror. Cobra mirrors carry pp:tenant-gate = "child-cli" and pass through, so the damage was invisible in a tool count: 6 tools per connector were dead while the server still listed them. Those 6 are the entire offline-mirror surface (context, search, sql) plus the entire code-orchestration surface (<prefix>_search / _get / _execute) - exactly the capabilities this connector's own description says a plain read-only MCP does not ship. Measured over stdio before the fix: 6/6 returned isError with the gate message; after, all 6 reach their handler. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press 4.30.3 (issue #4157, PR #4171); this is the surgical back-port, byte-identical to what 4.30.3 emits. TestMCPUngatedInvocationUsesRealVerifier is the regression test that ships with the 4.30.3 template: it drives the wrapper with the REAL verifier (not the fake the other two tests install) and fails if the handler is blocked. Reverting either the fall-through or the test fails check_handfixes.py.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Already fixed in the press at 4.30.3 (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4171). A reprint on 4.30.3 or later regenerates both the fall-through and the conformance test, so this entry exists to keep the back-port from being dropped by a reprint on an older engine or by a regen-merge that resurrects the 4.30.2 body.

asserts.not_contains: NewToolResultError("MCP tenant gate is not configured")
